significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, for factual questions with semantically confusable distractors, the fact remains available while a blended retrieval key diverts attention and causes recall failure; this is chiefly a form-(ii) causal mechanism with a narrow form-(iii) predictive coupling in the claim that the diverted fraction "causally predicts per-example recall failure." It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a routing mechanism, fixing expectations for which distracted examples should fail and linking the irrelevant-context degradation documented by Shi et al. (2023) to the factual-recall circuitry studied by Geva et al. (2023), but it remains bounded to one failure class rather than decomposing multiple behaviors. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: failure would rule out this specific preserved-storage/attention-diversion account, although the compound claim could fail in several ways and would not by itself identify the alternative mechanism. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic alone would not earn this score; the increment is the specific diversion-to-failure coupling, but retrieval-versus-storage plus targeted repair is close to the competent default hypothesis for this topic.

reach.justification: The claim names two usable handles: "DiversionScore"—the fraction of retrieval attention assigned to distractors—and the training-free "attention re-focusing" intervention that down-weights distractor key/value contributions. The intervention is ex ante because it acts before the answer is emitted, giving auditors or inference-system builders an action window, although its practical reach depends on identifying which span is genuinely irrelevant. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction that greater diversion implies greater failure risk should survive as a relation, while the particular retrieval heads and numerical calibration need not transfer; the asserted scope covers factual retrieval under lexical, categorical, and relational distractors in LLMs, not unrelated knowledge failures or non-AI domains. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic knowledge retrieval supplies neither the named diagnostic nor the inference-time control, so the reach comes from claim-specific handles.
